newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai gold imports surge to new high in January.
newsitem.headline: Dubai gold imports surge to new high in January.

text.p: Gold imports into Dubai soared to a record 46.35 tonnes in January, a 92.6 percent increase over January 1996, the World Gold Council (WGC) reported on Sunday.
Strong Indian demand, the Moslem holiday of Ramadan and gold prices at three-year lows were highlighted by WGC as the factors behind last month's strong import performance.

"The Middle East and India region is the fastest growing region in terms of demand for gold and Dubai is playing the role of the perfect hub for supply," said Rolf Schneebeli, WGC's chief executive for Middle East and India.
Fears of further gold selling by central banks in January sent gold prices last month to $345 an ounce, its lowest level for 3-1/4 years which prompted heavy demand in the Dubai market.

New Indian import regulations at the start of this year, allowing non-resident Indians to double the amount of gold that they could bring into India every six months, also led to a surge in Dubai import requirements, traders said.
Dubai is the main feed supplier to the India market, the world's largest consumer of the yellow metal.
Dubai's main supplier in January was Switzerland at 32.79 tonnes, WGC figures showed.
Imports into the Gulf emirate totalled 350.48 tonnes in 1996 and 318.03 tonnes in 1995.
The previous monthly import high was November 1996 when imports reached 35.50 tonnes.
